title: cats1: policy, config and kit
summary: etc/cats1.policy turns Tom's standing rule into deny lines for every principal: Firewall, Keys, Forwarder, Host reboot, and run:nft iptables ssh-keygen systemctl reboot shutdown. Xtpd is denied until Tom adds an allow line (allow codex Xtpd bringup /etc/xtpd/xtpd.conf). Codex may submit jobs and remove files in /var/lib/newshell/work, nothing else. etc/agent.conf provides mu, net, svc, xtpd, host and ws. The cats contract forbids build tools on cats1, so the compile chain is a demonstration elsewhere, not a cats1 job. The kit (newshell-kit-v0.1-dev5-jammy.tar.gz, sha256 ad6207e3830f847d64873c6f89a2b92d7e5f2219c3f1d81b8b0983adda094c33) is built in the jammy chroot; tests/kit_selftest.sh is read-only (temporary state and config) and passed there.
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: Never without Tom's explicit yes: change a firewall, rotate or copy a key, replace the WAN forwarder, reboot a host
Port 22 stays open until SSH over XTP has survived a reboot
Installing the kit on cats1 is an order marked NEEDS TOM'S DIRECT APPROVAL
procedure: Verify the kit from / (sha256sum -c opt/newshell/SHA256SUMS), check ldd, run tests/kit_selftest.sh as root
